name: Off-road vehicles, lifting and mobile machinery
note: For off-road vehicles and mobile machinery, CBP generally treats the fabrication and welding of the primary structural frames, chassis, and heavy working structures (such as booms, arms, lifting platforms, and drums) from raw metal as origin-conferring, or recognizes complex vehicle assembly when paired with the local fabrication of major structural subassemblies. Conversely, CBP treats bolting, fastening, and wiring imported drive motors, engines, electronics, and pre-fabricated frames together as simple assembly that does not confer origin. For jacks, an engine crane and a winch (version 2) the rulings turn on where the lifting mechanism and the structure were made, and point both ways: floor jacks took the origin of the country that cast and machined their hydraulic power units and welded their frames, while a bottle jack stayed Chinese, where its castings and pump were made, though Thailand machined and assembled them. No single part always decides. Not for hand tools, stands that only hold a raised load, or 3D printers. Written from 13 CBP substantial-transformation rulings outside every development and held-out split (D660), with six lifting rulings from the train pool added in version 2 (D826); every cited ruling was checked against its facts and holding. Costs are illustrative defaults; users edit them.

groups.name: Chassis and frame
operations: Saw, laser cut, stamp, punch, drill, and bend metal tubes, plates, and profiles
Align and weld structural metal elements in fixtures to form the chassis or lower frame weldment
Shot blast, polish, pre-treat, powder coat, and paint the structural frame

precedent.note: CBP consistently places decisive weight on where the foundational chassis or frame is cut, shaped, and welded from metal stock (N334276, N336445, N344843, N349019). Floor jacks took the origin of the country that welded and coated their frames and lift arms along with casting their power units (N333646, N347256).

groups.name: Booms, arms and working frames
operations: Cut, machine, press, and bend steel tubing and plates for lifting arms, booms, drums, or handling frames
Weld structural elements to form the upper frame, scissor arm, excavator boom, roller drum, or ROPS
Assemble mechanical lifting mechanisms, rollers, platforms, and material trays onto the upper structure

precedent.note: Producing major upper structural and working subassemblies confers origin when combined with chassis production or final integration (N334276, N337356, N340482), whereas sourcing only a single structural arm from a country is insufficient (N334276). A scissor jack's arms and screw rod (N348905) and an engine crane's post and boom (N348514), made in Thailand, were part of what made them Thai.

groups.name: Lifting mechanism and hydraulic power unit
operations: cast or forge the power unit base, piston head and pump body
assemble the hydraulic power unit with its cylinder, piston rod, valves and seals, fill it with oil and load test it
stamp and rivet scissor arms, roll-thread the screw rod and build the lift assembly
assemble the winch motor, drum and gearbox

precedent.note: Making the lifting mechanism was part of what decided origin for floor jacks whose hydraulic power units were cast and machined in Vietnam or Thailand (N333646, N347256), an engine crane whose power unit was forged and machined in Thailand (N348514), a scissor jack whose arms and screw rod were made in Thailand (N348905), a guided vehicle with a Korean lift assembly (N343416) and a winch with a Thai motor and drum and a Chinese gearbox (N346297). A bottle jack stayed Chinese, where its base and piston head were cast and its pump assembly made (N344692); the machining of those castings is the next group. A Chinese lifting mechanism did not decide for two guided vehicles whose frames were made in Korea (N337718, N340047).

groups.name: Machining of lift castings and tubes
operations: machine, drill and thread imported castings into the power unit base and piston head
cut and machine imported tubes into the cylinder and outer sleeve

precedent.note: Machining, drilling and polishing Chinese castings and tubes in Thailand was not enough: the bottle jack stayed Chinese (N344692).

groups.name: Powertrain and controls
operations: Produce or pre-assemble engines, drive motors, reducers, axles, and hydraulic systems
Assemble battery packs from cells and prepare controllers, sensors, and communication modules
Pre-assemble steering gears, radiators, fuel tanks, and handlebar or brake pedal subassemblies

precedent.note: Pre-assembling subassemblies does not confer origin when the structural frame is fabricated elsewhere (N336445, N344843, N349019), unless accompanied by comprehensive multi-part vehicle assembly and programming (N348937).

groups.name: Final assembly
operations: Bolt and fasten drive motors, engines, axles, suspensions, wheels, and casters to the chassis
Mount controllers, batteries, sensors, cameras, and operator cab or seat components
Join upper working structures or lifting assemblies to the lower chassis frame
Route and connect power, communication, and hydraulic lines, program ECUs, and inspect the vehicle
Pack the parts unassembled, with hardware, for assembly by the buyer

precedent.note: Final assembly confers origin when the assembly country also fabricates key structural frames or integrates complex drive and handling subassemblies (N337356, N337718, N340047, N348937), but bolting and wiring components onto pre-fabricated frames imported from another country is not enough (N336445, N344843, N349019). Welding the cylinder and pump to the base, pressing in the piston, filling, painting and testing in Thailand did not change a bottle jack's Chinese origin (N344692).
